description: Environment setup, REAL font acquisition (no fallbacks), and project reorganization scaffold for SECONDARY school level (council + region), preserving the existing lakezone example as the success reference. Establish the shared conventions every later feature depends on.
steps: Run `pyenv global 3.11.15` and `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Add `pymupdf>=1.24` to requirements.txt (used for PDF inspection during data extraction) and install it.

Confirm the existing lakezone example renders unchanged: `python -m sars_pdf.render data/lakezone_f2_mock_aug2026.json --pdf output/report.pdf --html output/report.html` succeeds and `python scripts/compare.py` runs (original.pdf still absent is fine). Do NOT modify any existing lakezone file.

FONTS (no fallbacks): the input PDFs embed ArialMT, Arial-BoldMT, ArialNarrow-Bold, TimesNewRomanPS-BoldMT. Genuine Monotype Arial/Times cannot be legally redistributed. Create a repo-local fonts/ directory and download metric-compatible open fonts as the real font FILES: Liberation Sans (Regular+Bold) as the Arial family, Liberation Sans Narrow (Bold) as Arial Narrow Bold, and Liberation Serif Bold (or Tinos Bold) as Times New Roman Bold. Verify checksums/downloads succeeded. Create fonts/README.md documenting exactly which file backs which family name and WHY (licensing decision point: no genuine Arial/Times available in-sandbox; substitutes are metric-compatible). If a genuinely licensed Arial/Times file can be obtained, prefer it and note the source.

Create a shared @font-face stylesheet at reports/_shared/fonts.css that maps EXACT family names to the real files with NO fallback chain: `@font-face { font-family:'Arial'; src:url('.../LiberationSans-Regular.ttf'); }` (and Bold), `@font-face { font-family:'Arial Narrow'; font-weight:bold; src:url('.../LiberationSansNarrow-Bold.ttf'); }`, `@font-face { font-family:'Times New Roman'; font-weight:bold; src:url('.../LiberationSerif-Bold.ttf'); }`. Each report's CSS will @import or copy this and reference a single family name (e.g. `font-family:'Arial';`) with no fallback list.

Create the reorganized directory tree under reports/: reports/secondary/council/ and reports/secondary/region/ (each will hold one subdir per report added in later features). Create reports/primary/README.md as a documented PLACEHOLDER for the future primary school level (no data, no templates - explain it is intentionally empty and mirrors the secondary structure).

Create reports/README.md explaining the new layout, the naming convention (LEVEL + WHAT-IT-DOES, not location/proper-noun, e.g. council-schools-rank-subjectwise), the self-contained-per-report rule, the shared fonts.css, the data-as-display-strings rule, and that generation is data-driven so any future data with the same shape renders through the same template. Cross-link to the top-level README's success example.
Extract inputs if not already present: `unzip -o council_pdf.zip -d council_pdf` and `unzip -o region_pdf.zip -d region_pdf`.

Update .gitignore if needed so extracted council_pdf/ and region_pdf/ working dirs are handled per project convention (do not commit the raw extracted PDFs unless they serve as reference/original.pdf copies; the ZIPs remain in the repo).
acceptance_criteria: `pip install -r requirements.txt` succeeds and pymupdf is importable.

The existing lakezone example still renders: `python -m sars_pdf.render data/lakezone_f2_mock_aug2026.json --pdf output/report.pdf` writes a PDF with no error, and no existing lakezone source file was modified.
fonts/ contains real .ttf files; `fc-scan` or fonttools confirms family names; reports/_shared/fonts.css references them with a single family name per @font-face and NO comma-separated fallbacks.
reports/secondary/council/, reports/secondary/region/, reports/primary/README.md, reports/README.md all exist with the documented conventions.
reports/primary/README.md clearly states it is a placeholder for future primary-level work.
verification: Run: pyenv global 3.11.15 && pip install -r requirements.txt && python -c 'import weasyprint, jinja2, pdfplumber, pypdfium2, PIL, fitz; print("deps ok")'
Run: python -m sars_pdf.render data/lakezone_f2_mock_aug2026.json --pdf output/report.pdf --html output/report.html && echo lakezone-ok
Confirm no comma-separated font fallback remains in reports/_shared/fonts.css (grep for 'font-family' and check each maps to one name).
findings:
Env: pyenv 3.11.15; pip install -r requirements.txt OK (weasyprint 70.0). Added pymupdf>=1.24; all deps import (`import ... fitz` prints a deprecation warning, use `import pymupdf`). Lakezone renders unchanged; I restored output/report.pdf and output/pages/*.png after render/compare regenerated them (byte-level timestamp diffs only) so the committed success reference stays intact. Only requirements.txt + .gitignore changed among tracked files.

FONTS (real, no fallback): downloaded Liberation Sans Regular+Bold and Liberation Serif Bold from official liberation-fonts 2.1.5 release. Liberation Sans Narrow was DROPPED after the 1.07.x line, so LiberationSansNarrow-Bold.ttf was extracted from the archived Debian fonts-liberation 1:1.07.4-11 .deb (snapshot.debian.org by hash 1d4311e811a29f52a5be2c179100f85001c74d20). Host has NO xz binary: decompressed data.tar.xz via python lzma. No genuine Monotype Arial/Times obtainable in-sandbox; used metric-compatible Liberation substitutes and documented licensing in fonts/README.md (SIL OFL 1.1, LICENSE copied to fonts/LICENSE-Liberation.txt). fonttools-verified family names: 'Liberation Sans' (Regular/Bold), 'Liberation Sans Narrow' (Bold), 'Liberation Serif' (Bold).

CRITICAL WeasyPrint gotcha for later features: @font-face in reports/_shared/fonts.css is IGNORED unless a SINGLE shared FontConfiguration() is passed to BOTH CSS(string=..., font_config=fc) AND write_pdf(font_config=fc); otherwise text silently falls back to Noto Sans. With font_config wired correctly, the test PDF embeds Arial / Arial-Bold / Arial-Narrow-Bold-Condensed / Times-New-Roman-Bold (the real Liberation glyphs) - confirmed via pymupdf get_fonts(). render.py does not yet wire font_config; per-report generators (later features) must do so.

Scaffold: reports/_shared/fonts.css (one family name per @font-face, NO comma fallback - grep-verified), reports/secondary/council/ + reports/secondary/region/ (with .gitkeep), reports/primary/README.md (placeholder), reports/README.md (layout + LEVEL+FUNCTION naming, self-contained rule, display-strings, data-driven intent). Extracted council_pdf/ (2.1M) and region_pdf/ (3.6M) are COMMITTED to git (per user steering) so the ZIPs need not be re-extracted each time; .gitignore left unchanged (no exclusion). Per-report reference PDFs will live at reports/.../reference/original.pdf.
